reason: The skin is the only available action and advances the whale's construction.
expectation: I expect the paper to cover the frame, hopefully leaving access for the workings.

effect: The frame now has its paper skin; the service hatch is the next available fitting.
reaction: The result was straightforward, with no detail yet about access.
reason: The hatch is the only offered combination and should keep the workings reachable.
expectation: I expect the hatch to provide an opening for servicing the lift module.

effect: The hatch keeps the controller and counterweight accessible while preserving the whale's shape.
reaction: That access makes the hatch feel purposeful.
reason: The fins are the only offered combination and should complete more of the whale's shape.
expectation: I expect the stiffened fins to attach to the whale; I'm unsure whether they'll have a mechanical role.

effect: The fins provide the whale's shape, not lift; the tile supplies that.
reaction: The distinction is useful and clears up my uncertainty about the fins.
reason: The padded mount is the only offered combination and should prepare a place for the lift module.
expectation: I expect the mount to attach inside the whale and cushion the module.

effect: The whale now has a mount ready for the lift module.
reason: The lift module is the only offered combination and is needed to complete the goal.
expectation: I expect the module to fit into the padded mount, with its controls accessible through the hatch.

effect: The lift module is now fitted inside the whale; its controls still need an accessible stop.
reaction: The fitting was straightforward, though it gave no detail about the controls.
reason: The exterior stop-button extension is the only offered combination and should make the stop reachable.
expectation: I expect an accessible outside button that cuts power to the lift module.

effect: The completed whale places its weight below the lift tile and links the exterior button mechanically to the stop switch.
reaction: The final explanation made the placement and safety control more meaningful than the straightforward fittings suggested.

mostWorthwhile.text: Fitting the outside stop was most worthwhile: the result explained both the pushrod and why the battery and counterweight sit low.

leastWorthwhile.text: Fitting the mount was the least engaging moment; it produced a straightforward result without explaining much.

surprise.text: The fins are only for the whale silhouette, not lift. That distinction usefully separates the real structure from the invented tile.

arbitrary.text: None felt purposeless, but with only one combination offered at each step, the sequence involved little meaningful choice.

continue.text: I would probably continue to see the assembled fair in action. The final explanation was interesting, though I would hope for more decisions than this chapter offered.
